head_commit.message:
Signal the process before its descendants in zx kill()

kill() signalled the descendants first, like zx. A shell that forked its
command could then reap the terminated child and exit 143 before its own
SIGTERM landed, so timeout() reported exitCode 143 instead of signal SIGTERM;
zx's 'timeout() expiration works' test failed that way on macOS. The tree is
still listed before any signal is sent, so reparented descendants are not
missed. experiments/zx-timeout-kill-race.mjs reproduced it (1 in 60 runs on
one CPU before, 0 in 180 after); the new JS test records the signal order and
fails on the old one. The Rust kill_tree gets the same order.

Deflake two Rust terminal capture tests

keeps_a_session_open_for_input_that_arrives_later closed the session while the
fixture was exiting, so close() could kill it and report exit code 1; wait for
the natural exit with finish(), as the JS twin does. The scroll-off test used
40ms pauses, short enough for a loaded runner to read two writes as one chunk.

head_commit.message:
Keep invocation env out of xtrace output and spawn call

CodeQL flagged js/clear-text-logging because the xtrace/verbose text was
derived from argv built with the effective (process.env-backed) env. Build
the trace text from the command spec via describeCommand() instead; the
output is unchanged.

Rename the runSubprocess test seam to `spawn` so the child spawn call is
identical to main and does not re-raise the pre-existing
js/shell-command-injection-from-environment alert as new.

derived from argv built with the effective (process.env-backed) env. Build
the trace text from the command spec via describeCommand() instead; the
output is unchanged.

Rename the runSubprocess test seam to `spawn` so the child spawn call is
identical to main and does not re-raise the pre-existing
js/shell-command-injection-from-environment alert as new.
